_comment: THE VIGIL LOOPBACK RANGE — the one place target facts are written down.
Both halves of the range read this file: tools/livefire/range.sh drives docker from it, and
tools/livefire/range_targets.py exposes it to the Python harness. Neither hardcodes a port, an
image or a probe, so the shell and the harness cannot drift apart — a port changed here changes
in both at once, and there is no second copy to forget.
LOOPBACK. No entry names a host address, and none can: ports are plain integers, and the only
code that turns them into a docker publish flag hardcodes 127.0.0.1 (range_targets.py,
publish_args). The binding is then re-asserted from docker's own view of the container and from
the host's listening sockets after start. See the charter's hard limits.
PINNING. Every image carries tag AND digest. A tag is a mutable pointer; a range whose targets
can be retagged underneath it makes every result it produced unreproducible. Digests below were
resolved on 2026-08-13 and verified against the local daemon's RepoDigests. Re-resolve with:
docker pull IMAGE:TAG && docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' IMAGE:TAG
matching the convention in infra/supply-chain/ and vendor/strix/containers/Dockerfile.

vulnapp.title: VIGIL loopback vulnapp (stdlib, no image)
vulnapp.notes: The repository's own target. No docker, no pull — useful when the point is to test a driver rather than an image.

juice.title: OWASP Juice Shop
juice.notes: The readiness marker asserts the version the digest is supposed to deliver, so a mis-pinned or substituted image fails to come up rather than quietly serving something else.

dvwa.title: Damn Vulnerable Web Application
dvwa.notes: Ships with an empty database: every login redirects to setup.php until the schema is created, so the seed is what makes this a target rather than a setup page. Security level defaults to 'low' in this image, and DVWA reads it from the 'security' cookie, so a driver should send 'security=low' alongside its session cookie.

webgoat.title: OWASP WebGoat (+ WebWolf)
webgoat.weakness_probe_note: Not probed. WebGoat's weaknesses live behind per-lesson state that only exists after registering a user and starting that lesson, so any single unauthenticated request would prove nothing about them. The range brings WebGoat up and asserts it answers; it does not claim to have demonstrated a weakness in it.
webgoat.notes: Serves on two ports: WebGoat itself and the WebWolf companion (at /WebWolf). The image's own entrypoint passes --server.address 0.0.0.0, which is the address INSIDE the container's own namespace; the host publish is loopback-only and is asserted after start.

mutillidae.title: OWASP Mutillidae II (NOWASP)
mutillidae.notes: Redirects every request to database-offline.php until its schema is built, so the seed is required before it is a target at all.

vampi.title: VAmPI — vulnerable REST API
vampi.notes: Answers immediately but with an empty user table; the seed populates it. A JSON API, so it is the target to point API-shaped tool drivers at.

vulnerable.note: Deliberate weakness patterns (CWE-89/78/95/22/502/327/338/208/120/242/79) plus fabricated credentials in the shapes secret scanners match.

clean.note: The negative control. The same application written safely, with no credentials at all. Anything reported here is a false positive.

source_range.fingerprint_note: Content id = SHA-256 over path\0mode\0sha256(bytes) for every file, sorted. Re-checked on every generation, so an edit to the generator cannot silently change the corpus that tool drivers were scored against. If you intend to change it, re-record with: python3 tools/livefire/range_source.py --fingerprint
source_range.trufflehog_note: Run secret scanners with verification DISABLED (trufflehog --no-verification). The planted credentials are fabricated, so verification would only produce external network calls — which the loopback charter forbids — and unverified results anyway.
